title: Averages

steps.title: Average means equal share
steps.content: The arithmetic average is the total of all values divided by the number of values. It is the value each item would have if the total were shared equally.
steps.formula: Average = Sum of values ÷ Number of values
steps.tip: In placement problems, convert averages into totals as early as possible.

steps.title: Find a simple average
steps.prompt: What is the average of 14, 18, 22 and 26?
steps.explanation: Sum = 80. There are 4 values, so average = 80/4 = 20.

steps.title: Use total = average × count
steps.content: If the average of n numbers is A, their sum is n×A. When a value is replaced, update the total first, then divide by the count.
steps.example: Average of 5 numbers is 16, so total = 80. Replace 12 by 22: new total = 90, new average = 18.
steps.tip: When one number is added or removed, update both the sum and the count.

steps.title: Average after replacement
steps.prompt: The average of 6 numbers is 15. One number 10 is replaced by 22. What is the new average?
steps.explanation: Old total = 90. New total = 90−10+22 = 102. New average = 102/6 = 17.
hints: Subtract the removed value, add the new value, divide by the same count.

steps.title: Weighted average
steps.content: When groups have different sizes, average the combined total—not the two averages directly. Combined average = (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂)/(n₁ + n₂).
steps.example: 10 students average 60; 20 students average 75. Combined average = (600+1500)/30 = 70.

steps.title: Trace a combined average
steps.content: Recover each group total before combining.
steps.prompt: 10 students average 50 and 20 students average 65. What is the combined average?
hints: Weight by the number of students in each group.

steps.title: Update an average safely
steps.content: Replacement problems are total problems in disguise.
steps.prompt: Arrange the steps when one value is replaced in a known average.
options: Divide the new total by the same count
Subtract the removed value and add the new value
Read the original average and count
steps.explanation: Recover the total, adjust it, then divide by the unchanged count.
hints: Totals come before averages after a change.
Count stays the same in a pure replacement.

steps.title: Add a new observation
steps.prompt: The average of 4 numbers is 20. A fifth number 30 is added. What is the new average?
steps.explanation: Old total 80; new total 110; count becomes 5; average 22.
hints: Update both total and count when a value is added.
New average is not simply old average plus the new number.

steps.title: Catch the equal-weight error
steps.content: A student averages two class averages of 60 and 80 as 70 even though the classes have 10 and 30 students.
steps.code:
class_a_average = 60
class_a_size = 10
class_b_average = 80
class_b_size = 30
combined = (class_a_average + class_b_average) / 2
print(combined)
options: The larger class must pull the combined average closer to 80

feedback_by_option.2: Averages can be combined using weighted totals.

steps.explanation: Weight by group size; the combined average is 75.
hints: Rebuild the combined total before dividing.

questions.prompt: The average of 8 values is 12. What is their sum?
The average of 4 numbers is 20. A fifth number 30 is added. New average?
10 students average 50 and 20 students average 65. Combined average?
Average of 5 people is 24. A person aged 30 joins. New average?
Average of 6 numbers is 15. Replace 10 by 22. New average?

learning_objectives: Recover a total using average × count.
Update an average after adding or replacing a value.
Use weighted averages when groups have different sizes.
Reject equal-weight mistakes on unequal groups.

common_misconceptions.misconception: When one value changes, the average changes by the full difference.
common_misconceptions.correction: The average changes by the difference divided by the number of observations.

common_misconceptions.misconception: A combined average is always the average of group averages.
common_misconceptions.correction: Weight each group average by its size unless the groups are equal.

common_misconceptions.misconception: The average must be one of the observed values.
common_misconceptions.correction: An average can be a value not present in the original list.

worked_examples.explanation: Convert the average into a total before finding a missing value.

company_applications.practice: Track total and count separately before updating an average.
Calculate combined averages for unequal group sizes.
Explain how one new observation changes the group mean.

srs_cards.question: How do you recover total from average?
How do you handle a replacement in an average?
srs_cards.answer: Update the total by removing the old value and adding the new value, then divide by the same count.

srs_cards.question: When can you average two group averages directly?
srs_cards.answer: Only when the groups have equal sizes; otherwise use a weighted average.

quest.story: Service-company papers hide replacement and weighted-average traps inside short word problems. Recover totals before you trust an average.
quest.mission: Calculate means, recover totals, update averages after replacement and compare weighted groups.
success_criteria: Recover total from average and count.
Update an average after replacing one value.
Use weighted averages for unequal groups.
